tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Income Tax Assessment order received by the Company under under section 156 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 of Rs. 11,55,050 on account of disallowance of proportionate interest expenses. Along with the said Order, Income Tax Department has issued a Show Cause Notice(“SCN”) under section 274 read with section 270A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 dated March 11, 2025 for imposing Penalty for under-reporting income for Assessment Year 2023-24 basis the above disallowance.
tax_litigation.status: The Company had submitted the disclosure regarding the Income Tax Assessment order dated March 11, 2025 as per the requirement of Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations on March 13, 2025. The Company has filed an appeal before CIT (Appeals) on March 28, 2025 against the said order which is still pending. The Company had also filed a reply on March 29, 2025 against the Penalty Notice before the Assessing Officer (‘AO’) requesting to keep the Penalty Notice in abeyance till the disposal of the said Appeal.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Show Cause Notices ("SCN") dated July 8, 2025 / Demand Notice dated December 29, 2025 received by the Company under section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act,2017 and corresponding section of the Jharkhand GST Act, 2017 read with Section 20 of the IGST Act, 2017 (“the Act”), confirming the demand of Rs 32,83,687 and equivalent amount of penalty under section 74, along with interest under section 50 of the Act.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner, Central GST & Central Excise (Audit), Ranchi (Jharkhand)
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received a Demand Order (“Order”) dated December 29, 2025, from the Deputy Commissioner, Central GST & Central Excise, Ranchi for which the Company has duly submitted the disclosure as per the requirement of Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations on December 30, 2025. The Order inter-alia seeks tax payment on the Entitlement of Input Tax Credit availed by the Company and corresponding reconciliation with various parameters mentioned in the Order. Based on Legal advice, it has a strong case on merit. There is no impact on financials, operation or other activities of the Company pursuant to the receipt of Order.

timeline.summary: NCLT Allahabad dismissed applications and vacated the stay on the EGM requisition regarding director removals on 23 April 2026.
Jagran Prakashan convened an EGM for 29 May 2026 to consider removing seven independent directors and one whole-time director following NCLT stay vacation.
Jagran Media Network Investment Private Limited disclosed no encumbrance by promoters or promoter group as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
On May 8, 2026, Jagran Prakashan informed exchanges that NCLT Allahabad re-notified company petitions to May 13, 2026.
On 13 May 2026, the NCLT Allahabad Bench heard arguments in company petitions C.P. No. 64 of 2023 and C.P. No. 57 of 2025 and re-notified the matters to 1 June 2026.
On 14 May 2026, NCLAT listed the appeals filed by JMNIPL and Jagran Prakashan for hearing on 22 May 2026 regarding board removal disputes.
Jagran Prakashan circulated independent directors' representations ahead of the 29 May 2026 EGM regarding proposed board removals amidst promoter disputes.
NCLAT completed hearings in Jagran Prakashan's appeal (C.A. 189/2026) reserving orders, while JMNIPL withdrew appeal C.A. 187/2026.
NCLAT allowed Jagran Prakashan's 29 May 2026 EGM to proceed but directed that resolution outcomes be kept in abeyance pending NCLT Allahabad's final decision.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹472.1 Cr (-1.9% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹16.98 Cr (against a loss of ₹15.8 Cr a year earlier).
On 29 May 2026, Jagran Prakashan released its investor presentation for Q4 and FY26 financial results.
Jagran Prakashan held its EGM on May 29, 2026, to vote on director removals, with implementation kept in abeyance per NCLAT orders.
Jagran Prakashan responded to BSE on June 3, 2026, regarding the delayed disclosure of EGM proceedings held on May 29, 2026.
On June 1, 2026, NCLT Allahabad adjourned promoter dispute petitions C.P. No. 64 of 2023 and C.P. No. 57 of 2025 to July 8, 2026.
Jagran Prakashan reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹499 Cr (+9% YoY) and PAT of ₹61 Cr (-8% YoY), with print ad growth offset by newsprint costs and radio profitability improving significantly
Jagran Prakashan reported that NCLT heard company petitions on October 26, 2026, and adjourned further arguments to December 3, 2026.
